title: Lazarus experience
description:
An experience is what a creator publishes: documentation, a prepared software environment, and the metadata needed to use it. It is authored as lazarus.yaml or lazarus.json, which are the same schema in two encodings (ADR-0016).

This schema is also a security boundary. It has no field for privileged mode, host mounts, host networking, docker.sock, added capabilities, or host namespaces. They are not disabled by default; they are unexpressible, so no request can ask for them (ADR-0015). Adding one is a security change and requires an ADR.

apiVersion.description: Schema version this experience was written against. Breaking schema changes require a new value here.

title.description: Short human title for the experience. Shown in the header and in a list of experiences.

description.description: One or two sentences describing what a reader will learn. Plain text; no markup.

tags.description: Free-form topical labels. Discovery only, never used for authorisation or policy.

documentation.description: The documents a reader works through, in order. Each is validated at publish time against the component allow-list (ADR-0017).

commands.description: Commands this experience documents. Declaring a command makes it discoverable and gives it a narrower policy evaluation. It never grants permission to run it: policy adjudicates every command at runtime, declared or not (ADR-0015).

tasks.description: Multi-step exercises. A task lists command references rather than raw command text, so the environment and docs stay the single source of truth.

secrets.description: Secrets this experience needs. An experience names a secret; it never carries one. Values are supplied out of band by an operator, encrypted at rest, redacted in every log and error, and never returned by any API.

policies.description: Tightening only. A policy entry can narrow what an experience may do; it can never widen it, and it cannot grant a capability policy would otherwise deny (ADR-0015).

imageDigest.description: A content-addressed container image reference. A tag is not an identity, so a digest is required and a tag alone is invalid.

portNumber.description: A TCP port, 1-65535. A value object rather than a bare integer, because the range is an invariant.

environment.description: The prepared software environment a session runs against.

workdir.description: Working directory inside the session layer. Relative paths only; '..' and absolute paths are rejected at validation, so a path containment check cannot be skipped by a manifest.

env.description: Non-secret environment variables. Secret values are never expressible here; use secrets[] by reference.

network.description: Egress policy. A session has no ingress route at all (ADR-0012), so only egress is expressible.

egress.description: Permitted outbound destinations. Absent means deny all outbound.

dns.description: Permitted DNS resolvers. Absent means the platform default.

resources.description: Upper bounds for a session's container. Every field is required when the object is present, because an omitted bound would silently mean 'unbounded' and deny-by-default has no way to tell that apart from an intent.

document.description: One document in the reading order.

id.description: Stable identifier referenced by commands and tasks. Unique within the experience.

mdx.description: The document body, authored as a restricted MDX subset: prose, headings, code, and allow-listed components with typed string and number props. Creator import, export, expressions, and arbitrary JSX are not supported, so there is no path from a document to eval (ADR-0017). Validated at publish time; a document that fails is never published.

command.description: A command the experience documents. The command is a list of arguments, never a shell string: there is no shell in the product to inject into (ADR-0013).

id.description: Stable identifier. Unique within the experience.

executable.description: The program to run. An absolute path or a bare name resolved against the image's PATH by the runtime.

args.description: Default arguments. A reader may change them; these are the values that populate the draft.

summary.description: One line saying what the command does. Shown on hover.

documentId.description: The document this command is explained in, if any.

expectsOutput.description: Whether the command is expected to print to stdout. Used for documentation quality, never for policy.

task.description: An ordered set of steps accomplishing one goal.

steps.description: Command ids in order. Each must resolve to a command in this experience.

secretRef.description: A reference to a secret by name. Never a value.

name.description: Logical name, unique within the experience.

envVar.description: Environment variable the value is exposed as inside the session.

required.description: Whether the session fails to start when the value is absent.

policyTightening.description: A restriction an experience may impose on itself. Tightening only. There is deliberately no field here that widens a capability, because a creator-supplied widening would be an untrusted input granting privilege.

effect.description: The restriction this entry applies. Deny is the only permitted value: an allow here would be a capability grant.

kind.description: A discriminated union rather than an optional flag, so a reader cannot be unsure which shape applies.

value.description: The literal to match, interpreted according to kind. A leading '*' matches a prefix.
